en.name: Francis de Sales
en.summary: Bishop of Geneva and Doctor of the Church whose gentle, accessible writings on holiness reached ordinary laypeople, not just clergy.
en.body: Francis de Sales trained as a lawyer before choosing the priesthood, and as a young priest undertook a difficult mission preaching Catholicism in a region of Savoy that had turned largely Calvinist, reportedly writing his arguments on pamphlets and slipping them under doors when parishioners refused to receive him in person. As bishop of Geneva he became renowned for a preaching and pastoral style built on patience and gentleness rather than confrontation, famously advising that "more flies are caught with honey than with vinegar." His book Introduction to the Devout Life, written for a laywoman rather than clergy, was revolutionary in insisting that deep holiness was possible in ordinary secular life, not only in convents and monasteries, and it remains a widely read spiritual classic. He co-founded the Order of the Visitation with Jane Frances de Chantal. He died in 1622 and was declared a Doctor of the Church in 1877.
